title: Allen Dulles cuts off Ruth Paine's Warren Commission testimony

tellings.quote: Alan Dulles is part of that committee hearing. He stops her.
Apparently, Dulles did not want the fact that Ruth Paine had actually been at the summer house or whatever.
tellings.difference: Says outright that what Dulles was hiding was her presence at the summer house, and credits Mary Bancroft.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe Dulles keeping Ruth Paine's testimony from revealing her stay at the summer house with his mistress's circle. This matches Levenda's account of Dulles stopping her at the Warren Commission hearing.

as_told.title: Dulles hides Ruth Paine's visit to the summer house

plain: In 1964, during hearings of the Warren Commission, the official inquiry into President Kennedy's assassination, the commission member Allen Dulles is said to have cut off the testimony of a witness named Ruth Paine. If true, it would suggest he was steering what went on the record. The author Peter Levenda tells it from the commission's published volumes, saying simply, "He stops her." Michels comes back to it in a later episode and says what Dulles was supposedly hiding. "Apparently," he says, Dulles did not want it known that Paine "had actually been at the summer house." He links that detail to a woman named Mary Bancroft. Levenda points to the record itself, while Michels adds a reason for the interruption.
